key_insight: A stable bulk iodide double perovskite, Cs2AgBiI6, can be synthesized by converting phase-pure Cs2AgBiBr6 through complete halide exchange after removing trace moisture.
engineering_relevance: This provides a lead-free, all-inorganic absorber candidate for solar and optoelectronic devices, with demonstrated microcrystal and thin-film processability.
method: Prepare phase-pure Cs2AgBiBr6 microcrystals as the precursor
Eliminate trace moisture to enable full Br→I anion exchange to Cs2AgBiI6
Deposit Cs2AgBiBr6 films by flash thermal evaporation, then convert to phase-pure Cs2AgBiI6 films
evidence_signal: The synthesized Cs2AgBiI6 shows broad visible absorption, a 1.70 ± 0.05 eV optical bandgap, near-IR photoluminescence at 1.03 eV, and photoconductivity in films.
watch_item: The material’s synthesis and phase purity are highly sensitive to moisture control, so handling and processing must remain rigorously dry.
paper_title: Synthesis of the Elusive Bulk Iodide Double-Perovskite Semiconductor, Cs2AgBiI6: Microcrystals and Photoconductive Films
